products.example: A subscription tier for small teams

content.title: The content pipeline
content.why: Every topic you plan to publish, with the caption, the thread and the hashtags already written when the day comes.

feedback.title: What your users are telling you
feedback.why: One row per piece of feedback, sorted by sentiment and priority — the ones that repeat are your roadmap.

analytics.title: The numbers you actually watch
analytics.why: Pick the handful of metrics that decide something and log them regularly — a number without a history means nothing.

automation.title: The work you stop doing by hand
automation.why: Name a task you repeat and this drafts the workflow and the tools for it, with the hours saved written next to it.

websites.title: Every site you are planning
websites.why: One row per site — the brief, the address and where it stands — so nothing important lives only in a browser tab. It does not build them.
websites.example: Landing page for the spring launch

apps.title: Every app on the list
apps.why: What it does, which platform it targets and how far along it is — from first sketch to live in the store. It does not build apps for you.

images.title: The images you need made
images.why: Keep the prompt, not just the picture — a prompt you can read again is a prompt you can improve next time. It does not create images.
images.example: Product photo on a white background

videos.title: The videos you have planned
videos.why: The brief for each video and how far it has got, so a shoot list is never something you keep in your head. It does not create videos.

presentations.title: A place to keep track of presentations
presentations.why: Note the decks you are planning or have already given — this page does not generate slides for you. Use the button above to add one.
presentations.example: Investor deck for the seed round

campaigns.title: Every campaign, and what it cost
campaigns.why: Channel, budget and status side by side, so the next budget decision is made from numbers rather than from feel. It does not run campaigns.

create.understanding: Working out what you asked for…

aiSteps.watchFailed: Progress can't be shown right now — the work continues in the background.

out_of_credits.what: You have run out of credits
out_of_credits.next: Buy a credit pack or move to a bigger plan, and the same action will go through — nothing you have written is lost.

rate_limited.what: Too many of these in the last hour
rate_limited.next: There is an hourly cap on this action so one account cannot spend the shared budget. Wait a few minutes and try again — the cap slides, it does not reset on the hour.

timeout.what: This took too long and was stopped
timeout.next: Long jobs have a ceiling so a stuck one cannot run forever. Try again with a shorter or more specific request — that usually finishes well inside it.

network.next: Check your connection and try again. If the work had already started it is still running in the background — reload the page rather than starting a second one.

credits.refunded: The credits held for this have been returned.
credits.charged: The credits for the work already done have been used.

agents.is: An agent is a job that runs on a schedule without you.
agents.does: You describe the task once; it runs when you told it to, emails you the result and keeps a history of every run.
agents.doesNot: It does not run without limit. There is a cap on runs per hour and on how many agents your plan allows, and every run costs credits.

websiteBuilder.is: A whole website, generated from a description.
websiteBuilder.does: It writes the pages, the copy and the layout from what you describe, and you keep changing it in plain words.
websiteBuilder.doesNot: It does not put anything on the internet. A generated site stays private until you publish it yourself.

published.is: The sites you have made live.
published.does: Publishing gives a site an address anyone can open, and counts its visitors here.
published.doesNot: It does not give you a domain of your own. The address is a path on this site today, not yourdomain.com — pointing a real domain at it is separate.

files.is: Your documents, readable by the AI.
files.does: Upload a PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or text file; the text is pulled out and you can ask questions across the ones you pick.
files.doesNot: It does not read scans. A PDF that is a photo of a page has no text to extract and needs OCR first, and very long documents are read up to a limit.

deepResearch.is: Research that would cost you several hours.
deepResearch.does: It shows you its plan first, then goes and does the work and comes back with sources you can check.
deepResearch.doesNot: It does not answer while you wait. It runs in the background — leave the page, close the tab, it keeps going and is here when you return.

memory.is: One search across everything you have logged.
memory.does: It looks through every module at once — ideas, leads, expenses, trades, sites — and takes you straight to the entry.
memory.doesNot: It does not store your conversations, and it keeps nothing of its own. Everything here is something you wrote in a module; nothing is added by the AI.

mission.is: One goal, broken into dated steps.
mission.does: You write the goal; it produces a plan you can tick off, and any step can be handed to the AI or scheduled for a day.
mission.doesNot: It does not carry itself out. A plan sits still until you run a step or schedule one — nothing happens because time passed.

integrations.is: Your own accounts, connected so the AI can read from them.
integrations.does: Gmail and Google Drive are connected read-only. Slack reads the channels you invite the app into, and agents can post results back there.
integrations.doesNot: It does not send your email, reply on your behalf, or delete anything. It never sees private Slack channels or direct messages.

team.is: The people who share this workspace with you.
team.does: You invite by email; each person signs in with their own account and sees the same data.
team.doesNot: It is not free and it is not your login. Seats are billed per person, and nobody ever needs your password.

timeline.is: Everything you have done, newest first.
timeline.does: It writes itself from every module, so you can answer "what did I actually do last month" without opening five pages.
timeline.doesNot: You do not write here. It is a record, not a diary — entries appear because you logged them elsewhere, and the order is when they happened.

favorites.is: The short list you built by pressing stars.
favorites.does: Anything you star anywhere shows up here, grouped by where it came from, so the few you keep returning to are one click away.
favorites.doesNot: Starring does not copy or move anything. These are the same entries, shown twice — edit one here and you have edited the original.

marketplace.is: Where people will share the agents, site templates and workflows they have built.
marketplace.does: Nothing yet. This page is a placeholder for a feature that has not been built.
marketplace.doesNot: It is not empty because of your plan, and upgrading will not open it. The button below is disabled because there is nothing behind it.

settings.is: Your account: the plan you are on, the credits you hold, and everything you have logged.
settings.does: Change your plan, buy credits, set the language and theme, name the assistant, and download every record in the account as one file.
settings.doesNot: It does not hold your records — each module keeps its own. And Delete account is not a way to clear them and start again: it ends the account, takes everything with it, and there is no undo. Export first.

offline.next: Check your connection and try again.

unknown.next: Try again, and contact support if it happens twice.
